default.title: Solid-state cells reach 400 Wh/kg in pilot lines
default.content: A pilot line has produced solid-state cells with an energy density of 400 Wh/kg, about 60 percent above typical lithium-ion cells. The cells were tested for 800 charge cycles.

default.title: Why solid-state batteries are still expensive
default.content: Solid-state cells cost roughly three times more than lithium-ion cells because ceramic electrolytes are hard to manufacture at scale. Analysts expect costs to fall below 150 dollars per kWh only after 2030.

default.title: Automakers announce solid-state timelines
default.content: Two large automakers plan small-volume cars with solid-state packs by 2027. Mass-market models are not expected before 2030.

default.title: Dendrite growth remains the main failure mode
default.content: Lithium dendrites can pierce the solid electrolyte at high charging rates and cause short circuits. Researchers report that a thin interlayer reduces this failure by about half.

default.title: Safety claims for solid-state packs
default.content: Solid-state packs do not use flammable liquid electrolytes, which lowers fire risk. Independent crash testing data is still limited.
